description.narrative: (USAID Central Africa Regional): Illicit trade in wildlife undermines biodiversity and security in Central Africa, where well-armed, well-organized networks of criminals exploit porous borders and weak institutions to profit from trading in poached wildlife. There is also widespread evidence that groups who trade in wildlife products also trade in other illicit products such as precious minerals and arms and may also engage in human trafficking. USAID's Protected Garamba-Chinko Protected Area Program will directly support the management of the Garamba National Park in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the Chinko Nature Reserve in the Central African Republic (CAR). This activity leverages substantial private financial and technical resources from outside the country and builds the capacity of local parks management agencies in both countries at the local and national level. FY 2022 Biodiversity funding will be used to strengthen wildlife law enforcement and security by supporting park rangers, developing protected area management capacity, and engaging within the surrounding community to provide incentives and increase support for conservation. The vehicle for this assistance will be technical assistance, training, procurement of materials and support of outreach work to the protected area management structures in Garamba National Park and Chinko Nature Reserve....This activity will contribute to maintaining the ecological integrity of the humid forest ecosystem of the Congo Basin, which is vital to regional stability and a U.S. foreign policy priority. It contributes to the Joint Strategic Plan Strategic Objective 2.2: (Promote healthy, educated and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives) by protecting natural resources critical to long term, sustainable growth, and food and water security....... .
